status: exploratory whole-process comparison; not a controlled throughput benchmark
working_tree_note: Both binaries used the same uncommitted packed-input compiler; only the verifier's validateCompiledKey call differed.

program.relation: four public M31 lanes; 256 rounds of x := x*x + 7

build.baseline_change: Copy mvp_runtime.zig and remove only `try validateCompiledKey(allocator, source, key, program_digest);` from validateKey. Copy build.zig and mvp_verifier_main.zig with their root imports pointed at that runtime copy. Compile with the same source, embedded verification key, gate lowering, Zig version, and ReleaseFast setting.

method.clock: Python time.perf_counter around subprocess.run; includes process startup, source-to-key validation, proof decoding, and STARK verification
method.order: current then baseline on even-indexed pairs; baseline then current on odd-indexed pairs
method.warmup: No separate warmup. The first cold invocation for each binary is present in samples; the median is robust to it.

interpretation: For this gate-heavy relation and one-proof-per-process CLI, recompiling the embedded source and recomputing its fixed circuit commitment added about 56 ms of verifier wall time. It does not change prover time. Absolute latency and overhead for other relations or machines are not established by this observation.
